advances: Fixed proper barycentric caps on a physical simplex. The groups need not be concurrent, and no sign is asserted for signed multipliers or moving thresholds.

proof:
Near the reference, the cap in direction $i$ contains just the $i$th vertex, and its edge ratios from that vertex are $(W_{ii}-a)/(W_{ii}-W_{ij})$ for $j\ne i$. The affine map $W$ preserves the sum of coordinates and acts identically on the one-dimensional quotient, so the moving volume is $V\det W$ (the determinant is positive near $I$). Hence
$$\frac{F_{i,a}(W)}{V}=\det W\,\frac{(W_{ii}-a)^d}{\prod_{j\ne i}(W_{ii}-W_{ij})}.$$
Along $W=I+tB$, the first and second log derivatives at zero are
$$T+s_i+d(X-1)b_i,\qquad
-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)-dX^2b_i^2+\sum_{j\ne i}(b_i-A_{ij})^2.$$
The first derivative of $L/V$ is $T(1-\sum_i e_i)-\sum_i(e_i s_i+\chi_i b_i)$. Since $b_j=-\sum_{i\ne j}A_{ij}$, the independent coefficient of $A_{ij}$ is $-1+\sum_l e_l-e_i+\chi_j$. At stationarity, comparing two distinct rows with a third index as column forces all $e_i=e$ (here $m\ge3$); substituting gives $\chi_i=1-de$. Conversely these equations make each coefficient zero. Nonnegativity of all weights prevents $e=0$ at stationarity, and then $X>1$ gives $\chi_i>0$, hence $e<1/d$. Solving $\chi_i=de(\mu-1)$ gives $\mu=1/(de)$. The effective cap has normalized weight $e$ and reciprocal threshold $\mu$, so its weighted first derivatives agree vertex by vertex.

For a cap, divide its second derivative by its reference volume to get the second log derivative plus the square of the first. At a vertex the expectation of the latter square is its value at $\mu$ plus $d^2\sigma_i^2 b_i^2$, and the expectation of the second log derivative is its value at $\mu$ minus $d\sigma_i^2 b_i^2$. Subtract these contributions, multiplied by $e$, from the normalized volume second derivative $T^2-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)$. This gives the two formulas and, since $d(d-1)e>0$, the equality condition.

statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, and let the reference labeled simplex of volume $V>0$ have vertex matrix $I$ in barycentric coordinates. In each direction $i$, take finitely many fixed proper caps $\xi_i\ge a_{gi}$, $0<a_{gi}<1$, with multipliers $\ell_{gi}\ge0$. For column-sum-one $W$ near $I$, let $F_{gi}(W)$ be the actual cap volumes and $L(W)=V\det W-\sum_{gi}\ell_{gi}F_{gi}(W)$. Define
$$
X_{gi}=\frac1{1-a_{gi}},\quad \eta_{gi}=\ell_{gi}(1-a_{gi})^d,\quad
e_i=\sum_g\eta_{gi},\quad \chi_i=d\sum_g\eta_{gi}(X_{gi}-1).
$$
The Lagrangian is stationary over all physical vertex velocities if and only if $e_i=e>0$ and $\chi_i=1-de$ at every $i$. In this case $0<e<1/d$ and the distributions with weights $\eta_{gi}/e$ have common mean $\mu=1/(de)$ in $X$. The single-threshold model with threshold $a_*=1-1/\mu=1-de$ at every vertex and multiplier $e/(1-a_*)^d$ has the same first derivative as the multigroup Lagrangian. Let $Q_*(B)$ be its normalized Hessian, and let $\sigma_i^2=\operatorname{Var}_i(X)$ under the vertex $i$ weights. For each zero-column-sum $B$,
$$Q_{\mathrm{multi}}(B):=\frac{D^2 L(I)[B,B]}{V}
=Q_*(B)-d(d-1)e\sum_i\sigma_i^2 B_{ii}^2.$$
The correction is zero exactly when $B_{ii}=0$ for every $i$ with $\sigma_i^2>0$. With $b_i=B_{ii}$, $A$ the off-diagonal part of $B$, $s_i=\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}$, and $T=\operatorname{tr}B$, the effective Hessian is
$$
Q_*(B)=T^2-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)-e\sum_i
\left([T+s_i+d(\mu-1)b_i]^2-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)-d\mu^2 b_i^2+\sum_{j\ne i}(b_i-A_{ij})^2\right).
$$
title: Stationarity and reciprocal-threshold variance for fixed simplex caps
